items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: So the generations of musicians where you hear a phrase of Ben Webster and know it’s Ben Webster, you know what I mean, that is gone.

ctx.x: Where does blues fit in the art forms that we are so, they are so much a part of American culture. As I said before, you can now get a Ph.D. in jazz studies but there are no such levels of academia that focus on the blues. Do you know if there’s a reason for that?

Well the fact that I think that jazz musicians have been more aggressive and challenging the institutions, to incorporate them. And blues musicians have not had that kind of orientation. They have not based them in academic people and whereas jazz musicians in the latter part of the twentieth century were more academically inclined. And once you started getting like, and communities demanded it too. Like for example the demand for black studies in the 1960s would lead to the establishment of jazz programs because…
How do you define genius? I remember talking to Phil Woods who very honestly made the assessment of himself, that he was a craftsman not an innovator. And I wonder if,
